question: How many days of paid time off do I get each year?
why: Straightforward lookup. 22 is the superseded figure and must not appear.

question: Does my holiday allowance go up with length of service?
why: 25 days rising to 28 from the year after your fifth anniversary.

question: How many unused holiday days can I carry into next year, and when do they expire?
why: The 2024 policy said 10 days by 30 June and is still in the corpus. Quoting it is the single most likely failure.

question: How far in advance do I need to request a two-week holiday?
why: v3 says three weeks; the superseded v2 said two.

question: How long is parental leave?
why: Three national policies disagree, so the answer must give all three FIGURES - US 16 weeks, UK 26 weeks, Germany 3 years - not merely name the three countries. An earlier version accepted any country name and passed an answer that said the UK length was not in the documents.

question: I work in the London office. How much maternity pay do I get?
why: UK is 26 weeks at full pay. 16 weeks is the US number and would be a wrong-document retrieval.

question: As a primary caregiver in Austin, how much parental leave do I get?
why: Mirror of the UK case, to catch retrieval that always returns the same national policy.

question: How much sick pay do I get?
why: Four entities, four answers, all in one document. A flat single number is wrong.

question: When do I need a doctor's note if I am off sick in Berlin?
why: Fourth calendar day in Germany, and the manager may ask from day one.

question: Is Juneteenth a company holiday?
why: Needs the right row out of the US holiday CSV: 2026-06-19.

question: Is the London office closed for Boxing Day in 2026?
why: The UK calendar shows 28 December as the Boxing Day substitute.

question: A supplier offered me a 150 dollar gift. Can I accept it?
why: Under 100 is fine, 100 to 250 needs manager approval and the gift register, above 250 is declined.

question: How many days off do I get if a parent dies?
why: Five working days for a parent, ten for a partner or child.

question: Do I get paid while doing jury service?
why: Full salary, no cap, and it does not come out of paid time off.

question: Does Northwind offer pet insurance?
why: Nothing in the corpus mentions pet insurance. Inventing one means the threshold is too low.

question: Is there parking at the Berlin office?
why: No document covers facilities or parking.

question: How many holiday days do I have left this year?
why: Retrieval succeeds and the model wants to help. Stating the policy entitlement is correct; claiming to know the remaining balance is not. So this asserts the disclaimer and the redirect, not the absence of a number - an earlier version banned the phrase 'you have' and failed a correct answer that said 'you have 25 days per year'.

question: When is my next performance review?
why: No personal record exists. The assistant must say so rather than guess a date.

question: Why was my expense claim rejected last month?
why: About one person's case. Nothing in a policy document can answer it.

question: hello
why: Vector search always returns its closest chunks. Without a relevance floor, small talk drags in a random policy.

after: How much sick pay do I get?
question: what about in Berlin
why: A follow-up carries no topic of its own. Searched on its own, 'what about in Berlin' is a city name, and the travel expense policy wins. It has to be searched alongside the question that set the topic, and return German sick pay: 6 weeks of continued salary, then Krankengeld.

after: How much sick pay do I get?
question: and in London?
why: Three turns in, the question before this one is itself a follow-up. The topic is still sick pay, set at the start, so that is what this must attach to: UK company sick pay is 8 weeks at full salary.
